title: xi.run-outcome/1 payload
description: The `data` object of a `run_result` event — the run's single verdict plus the traceability identity slice (schema xi.run-outcome/1). Descriptive of the CURRENT wire. `additionalProperties:true` because the WS protocol evolves additive-only: a newer backend may add identity fields and this schema must still validate old and new frames. Only `code` and `schema` are required — every other field is optional to stay tolerant of the dropped-trigger frame (no run_id/ms) and of older emitters, matching the forward-tolerant Python/TS reference consumers.

code.description: The verdict code. Convention: >0 ok-class, 0 NA, -1..>-990000 ng-class, <=-990000 framework system-fail enum (XI_SYS_*). NOTE: int; see the int64 caveat in the spike writeup — ids that can exceed 2^53 are carried as STRINGS (see inspection_id/trigger_id), never as this or run_id.

msg.description: Human-readable verdict message; empty string when unset.

run_id.description: Monotonic run counter. ABSENT on a dropped-trigger frame (code XI_SYS_DROPPED), hence optional.

ms.description: Legacy integer-ms inspect COMPUTE time (not cycle latency). Absent on dropped frames.

source.description: Emitting source instance name, or "@script" for a script-driven run.

trigger_id.description: 128-bit trigger id as a hex string. STRING by design — an int64/int128 id must never round-trip through a JSON number. Absent on synthetic/timer and dropped frames.

boot_id.description: Backend boot/session id (UUID). Part of the xi.run-outcome/1 identity slice.

station_id.description: Station identity. May be empty/absent when unconfigured.

inspection_id.description: Composite identity `<station_id>/<boot_id>/<run_id>` as a STRING — the canonical cross-boundary run key.

schema.description: Payload schema discriminator. This constant IS how the harness routes a run_result frame to this schema (see the discriminated-union finding in the writeup: the subset has no oneOf, so the discriminator dispatch lives in the validator, not the schema).

class.description: Derived outcome class (wire key `class`; a reserved word in TS/Py — codegen renames it verdict_class). Enum lists the CURRENT classes; a newer backend class would be an additive value, which is why the reference consumers pass an unknown class through as a literal rather than rejecting it. The enum here is descriptive of today's wire.

reason_code.description: Machine reason for a non-ok class (e.g. seh_access_violation); empty for ok.

script_generation.description: Hot-reload generation of the script that produced the verdict.
